> **Note:** The content of this vignette was generated using Claude agents and then reviewed by package authors.

LEVANTE task scores are ability estimates from item response theory (IRT)
models fit with [`mirt`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=mirt). This
vignette shows how to fit those models for one task with `levantemodels`: what
the input data looks like, the calls that fit the models, and how to work with
the model files they write. (For scoring data against models that have
already been fit, see `vignette("scoring-and-model-registry")`.)

The vignette uses simulated data so that it runs offline in a few seconds. The
last section shows how to build the same input from real LEVANTE data.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(levantemodels)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

## Input data

The fitting functions take trial-level data **nested by task and by group**:
one row per combination of task and grouping variables, with the trials in a
list-column called `data`.

Here we simulate a 4-alternative task (`chance = 0.25`) given at two sites.
Children at `site_a` (English) saw 15 items, and children at `site_b` (German)
saw only the first 12 of them. Responses follow a 2PL model with a guessing
floor at chance.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(1)

items <- tibble(
  item_uid = sprintf("matrix_%02d", 1:15),
  a = rlnorm(15, 0, 0.3),              # discrimination
  b = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 15),     # difficulty
  chance = 0.25
)

simulate_site <- \(dataset, language, n_runs, theta_mean, item_uids) {
  tibble(dataset, language,
         run_id = paste0(dataset, "_run", 1:n_runs),
         theta = rnorm(n_runs, theta_mean)) |>
    cross_join(filter(items, item_uid %in% item_uids)) |>
    mutate(p = chance + (1 - chance) * plogis(a * (theta - b)),
           correct = runif(n()) < p) |>
    select(dataset, language, run_id, item_uid, chance, correct)
}

trials <- bind_rows(
  simulate_site("site_a", "en-US", 400, 0.0, items$item_uid),
  simulate_site("site_b", "de-DE", 300, 0.5, items$item_uid[1:12])
)

task_data <- trials |>
  mutate(item_task = "matrix") |>
  nest(data = -c(item_task, dataset, language))

task_data
```

Each element of `data` holds one row per trial:

```{r inner-data}
task_data$data[[1]]
```

The columns the fitting functions need are:

| Column | Level | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `item_task` | outer | task name, used to select a task and to name output files |
| grouping variable(s) | outer | e.g. `language`, `dataset`, `site`: what models are fit separately for, or what groups multigroup models compare |
| `run_id` | `data` | one task administration; each run becomes one row of the response matrix |
| `item_uid` | `data` | item identifier; an item that is answered more than once in a run is treated as several instances whose parameters are constrained to be equal |
| `correct` | `data` | response (logical or 0/1); `NA` responses are dropped |
| `chance` | `data` | chance level for the item, used as its fixed lower asymptote (guessing parameter) |

Before fitting, items with no variance in responses are dropped. For
multigroup models, items without variance within some group are also dropped.

## Specifying the models

Models are specified as a data frame with one row per model. For *pooled*
models (fit separately for each subset of the data) the columns are `nfact`
(number of factors) and `itemtype` (`"Rasch"` or `"2PL"`). For *multigroup*
models there's also `invariance`, which says what is constrained to be equal
across groups:

- `"configural"`: nothing is shared, so each group has its own item
  parameters.
- `"metric"`: slopes are shared.
- `"scalar"`: slopes and intercepts are shared, and group means and variances
  are freely estimated.

(See `invariances` for the mapping to `mirt` arguments.)

```{r models}
models_pooled <- tribble(
  ~nfact, ~itemtype,
       1,   "Rasch",
       1,     "2PL"
)

models_multigroup <- tribble(
  ~nfact, ~itemtype, ~invariance,
       1,   "Rasch", "configural",
       1,   "Rasch", "scalar",
       1,     "2PL", "configural",
       1,     "2PL", "metric",
       1,     "2PL", "scalar"
)
```

Priors are a named list: each name is a `mirt` parameter, and each value
gives the prior type and its two parameters. These are the priors that
LEVANTE uses:

```{r priors}
priors <- list(d = c("norm", 0, 3), a1 = c("norm", 1, 0.3))
```

## Fitting

The fitting functions write each fitted model to `registry_dir` as a
`ModelRecord` saved in an `.rds` file, and they are called for this side
effect. Models are fit with verbose `mirt` output, which we hide here.

```{r registry-dir, eval = FALSE}
registry_dir <- "model_registry"
```

```{r registry-dir-temp, include = FALSE}
# when building the vignette, write models to a temporary directory instead
registry_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "model_registry")
```

**Pooled models by language.** `fit_bylanguage_task()` fits every model in
`models_pooled` separately for each language in the data.
`fit_task_models_pooled()` does the same for a single subset of any
variable, e.g. `subset_var = dataset, subset_val = "site_a"`.

```{r fit-pooled, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
fit_bylanguage_task(task_data, models = models_pooled, priors = priors,
                    task = "matrix", registry_dir = registry_dir)
```

**Multigroup models.** `fit_task_models_multigroup()` fits one model with
every level of `group` as a group, for each row of `models_multigroup`:

```{r fit-multigroup, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
fit_task_models_multigroup(task_data, models = models_multigroup,
                           priors = priors, task = "matrix", group = dataset,
                           registry_dir = registry_dir)
```

Each multigroup specification is fit in up to two steps:

1. **`overlap_items/`**: a model fit to just the items that every group saw
   (here, the 12 items common to both sites).
2. **`all_items/`**: a model fit to all items. Parameters for the overlapping
   items are fixed at their values from step 1, so these items anchor the
   scale and the remaining items are calibrated onto it. This step is skipped
   for configural models, since they put no constraints across groups.

The resulting registry:

```{r registry-tree}
list.files(registry_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

Paths follow the pattern `{task}/{model_set}/{subset}/{task}_{itemtype}_f{nfact}[_{invariance}].rds`.
This is the same layout as the LEVANTE model registry on Redivis: each row of
the scoring table (`fetch_scoring_table()`) gives a `model_set`, `subset`,
`itemtype`, `nfact`, and `invariance`, and `model_spec_filename()` turns these
into a path in this layout.

## Working with model files

Each file contains a `ModelRecord`, a lightweight record of the fitted
model that holds its parameters, the data it was fit to, its fit statistics,
and the EAP ability scores for the data it was fit to.

```{r read}
mod_rec <- readRDS(file.path(registry_dir,
                             "matrix/multigroup_dataset/all_items/matrix_2pl_f1_scalar.rds"))
mod_rec
```

**Item parameters.** `mod_coefs()` returns one row per item and group, with
slope (`a1`), intercept (`d`), lower and upper asymptotes (`g`, `u`),
difficulty on the IRT scale (`-d / a1`), and the number of responses to the
item. Under scalar invariance the parameters are the same for both groups.
Items 13–15 have no responses from `site_b`, but they still get that group's
(shared) parameters.

```{r coefs}
mod_coefs(mod_rec)
```

**Ability scores.** `scores()` returns EAP ability estimates and their
standard errors for each run the model was fit to:

```{r scores}
scores(mod_rec)
```

As a check, the estimates approximately recover the simulated difference between sites
(`site_b` was simulated 0.5 SD higher):

```{r scores-by-site}
scores(mod_rec) |>
  mutate(group = mod_rec@groups) |>
  summarise(mean_ability = mean(ability), .by = group)
```

**Model comparison.** `AIC()`, `BIC()`, and `logLik()` work on a
`ModelRecord`. Models are only comparable when they're fit to the same data,
so here we compare the five `overlap_items` models:

```{r compare}
overlap_dir <- file.path(registry_dir, "matrix/multigroup_dataset/overlap_items")
overlap_files <- list.files(overlap_dir, full.names = TRUE)

tibble(model = basename(overlap_files),
       mod_rec = lapply(overlap_files, readRDS)) |>
  mutate(logLik = sapply(mod_rec, logLik),
         AIC = sapply(mod_rec, AIC),
         BIC = sapply(mod_rec, BIC)) |>
  select(-mod_rec) |>
  arrange(BIC)
```

**Other `mirt` functions.** A `ModelRecord` doesn't store the full `mirt`
model object. `model_from_record()` rebuilds it from the stored parameters
and data (without re-estimating anything), so you can use other `mirt`
functions, e.g. for item fit or plots:

```{r mirt}
mod <- model_from_record(mod_rec)
mirt::itemfit(mirt::extract.group(mod, group = "site_a"))
```

Other contents are available as slots, e.g. `mod_rec@data` (the response
matrix, with columns in `items(mod_rec)` order), `mod_rec@groups` (group of
each row), and `model_vals(mod_rec)` (the full `mirt::mod2values()`
parameter table).

## Using real LEVANTE data

To fit models to real data, build `task_data` from the raw (unprocessed)
per-site LEVANTE datasets. `process_trials()` loads their trials, drops
practice trials, incomplete runs, and invalid runs, and adds item identifiers
and metadata. Language comes from the run data and dataset from the
participant data, and `recode_trials()` then makes the trials ready for
scoring:

```{r real-data, eval = FALSE}
dataset_spec <- list(
  list(name = "pilot_western_ca_main_raw:97mt", version = "v15_28")
)

runs <- process_runs(dataset_spec)
participants <- process_participants(dataset_spec)

task_data <- process_trials(dataset_spec) |>
  left_join(runs |> select(run_id, language), by = "run_id") |>
  left_join(participants |> select(user_id, dataset), by = "user_id") |>
  recode_trials() |>
  nest(data = -c(item_task, dataset, language))
```

The production LEVANTE models also apply further exclusions before fitting
(e.g. duplicate runs, straightlining, responses that are too fast or too slow,
and items flagged for exclusion). These exclusions are applied in the
`levante-pilots` repository, in `01_fetch_data/02_scoring_prep.qmd`, and the
models are fit in `02_score_data/01_fit_irt/01_fit_irt_modular.qmd`, which
runs the fits above for every task in parallel.
